metadata.description: Common accessibility remediation patterns with code examples

patterns.name: Missing Alt Text (Informative Image)
patterns.description: Images that convey information need descriptive alt text that provides the same information.
patterns.notes: Alt text should describe the information the image conveys, not just what it looks like. For complex images like charts, consider also providing a data table.

patterns.name: Missing Alt Text (Decorative Image)
patterns.description: Decorative images that don't convey information should have empty alt or be hidden from assistive technology.
patterns.notes: Use empty alt="" (not missing alt) or role="presentation". Consider using CSS background-image instead for purely decorative images.

patterns.name: Complex Image Needs Long Description
patterns.description: Complex images like infographics, diagrams, or charts need extended descriptions beyond what fits in alt text.
patterns.notes: Options: Use aria-describedby pointing to visible text, a details/summary disclosure, or link to a separate page with full description.

patterns.name: SVG Missing Accessible Name
patterns.description: Inline SVGs need accessible names using title element and aria-labelledby.
patterns.codeAfter:
<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" role="img" aria-labelledby="icon-title">
  <title id="icon-title">Graduation cap</title>
  <path d="M12 2L2 7l10 5 10-5-10-5z"/>
</svg>
patterns.notes: For decorative SVGs, use aria-hidden="true". For informative SVGs, use role="img" with title element and aria-labelledby.

patterns.name: Form Input Missing Label
patterns.description: Form inputs need programmatically associated labels so assistive technology can announce them.
patterns.codeAfter:
<label for="email">Email:</label>
<input type="email" id="email" name="email">
patterns.notes: Use explicit label with for/id, or implicit label wrapping the input. Never rely on placeholder as the only label.

patterns.name: Form Error Not Identified
patterns.description: Form errors must be identified in text and the error description should suggest corrections.
patterns.codeBefore: Invalid
patterns.codeAfter: Please enter a valid email address (example: name@domain.com)
patterns.notes: Don't rely on color alone. Use aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby to associate error message. Describe what's wrong and how to fix it.

patterns.name: Required Field Not Indicated
patterns.description: Required fields must be indicated both visually and programmatically.
patterns.notes: Use the required attribute and/or aria-required="true". Visually indicate required fields and explain the indicator (e.g., "* indicates required").

patterns.name: Radio/Checkbox Group Missing Fieldset
patterns.description: Groups of related checkboxes or radio buttons need fieldset and legend to provide group context.
patterns.codeBefore: Preferred contact method:
patterns.codeAfter:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Preferred contact method:</legend>
  <input type="radio" name="contact" id="email"> <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input type="radio" name="contact" id="phone"> <label for="phone">Phone</label>
</fieldset>
patterns.notes: Screen readers announce the legend with each option, providing context. Also useful for grouping related text inputs.

patterns.name: Link Purpose Unclear
patterns.description: Link text should clearly describe the destination or purpose without relying on surrounding context.
patterns.codeAfter: Read our privacy policy
patterns.notes: Avoid generic link text like 'click here', 'read more', 'learn more'. The link text should make sense out of context.

patterns.name: Button Has No Accessible Name
patterns.description: Buttons must have an accessible name, especially icon-only buttons.
patterns.codeAfter:
<button onclick="deleteItem()" aria-label="Delete item">
  <svg aria-hidden="true"><!-- trash icon --></svg>
</button>
patterns.notes: Use aria-label, visually hidden text, or visible text. The accessible name should match or include any visible text (2.5.3 Label in Name).

patterns.name: Custom Control Missing Role
patterns.description: Custom interactive elements need appropriate ARIA roles, states, and keyboard support.
patterns.notes: Custom controls need: role, accessible name, state (if applicable), and keyboard operability. Prefer native HTML elements when possible.

patterns.name: Focus Indicator Not Visible
patterns.description: Interactive elements must have a visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
patterns.notes: WCAG 2.4.13 requires focus indicator of at least 2px perimeter with 3:1 contrast against unfocused state. Use :focus-visible to show focus only for keyboard users.

patterns.name: Missing or Improper Heading Structure
patterns.description: Pages should have a logical heading hierarchy starting with h1, without skipping levels.
patterns.codeAfter:
Products

Electronics

Laptop
patterns.notes: Use one h1 per page. Don't skip levels (h1 to h3). Headings should describe section content. Don't use headings just for visual styling.

patterns.name: Missing Landmark Regions
patterns.description: Use HTML5 landmark elements to define page regions for assistive technology navigation.
patterns.codeAfter:
<header>...</header>
<nav aria-label="Main">...</nav>
<main>...</main>
<footer>...</footer>
patterns.notes: Use semantic elements: header, nav, main, aside, footer. Only one main per page. Label multiple navs with aria-label.

patterns.name: Missing Skip Navigation Link
patterns.description: Provide a skip link to bypass repeated navigation blocks.
patterns.codeAfter:
Skip to main content
...
/* CSS */ .skip-link { position: absolute; left: -9999px; } .skip-link:focus { position: static; left: auto; }
patterns.notes: Skip link should be the first focusable element. Make it visible on focus. Target should have tabindex="-1" to receive focus in all browsers.

patterns.name: Missing or Non-Descriptive Page Title
patterns.description: Every page needs a unique, descriptive title that identifies its purpose.
patterns.codeAfter: <title>Contact Us - My Website</title>
patterns.notes: Format: 'Page Name - Site Name'. Title should be unique within the site and describe the page's specific content or purpose.

patterns.name: Focusable Element Inside aria-hidden
patterns.description: Elements with aria-hidden="true" should not contain focusable elements.
patterns.notes: aria-hidden="true" hides content from AT but doesn't prevent keyboard focus. Either remove aria-hidden or make children unfocusable.

patterns.name: Dynamic Content Not Announced
patterns.description: Dynamic content updates need ARIA live regions to announce changes to screen reader users.
patterns.notes: Use role="status" or aria-live="polite" for non-urgent updates. Use role="alert" or aria-live="assertive" for urgent/error messages.

patterns.name: Modal Dialog Focus Management
patterns.description: Modal dialogs must trap focus within the dialog and return focus when closed.
patterns.codeAfter:
Confirm

/* JavaScript needed to: 1. Move focus to dialog (or first focusable) on open 2. Trap Tab/Shift+Tab within dialog 3. Close on Escape key 4. Return focus to trigger element on close */
patterns.notes: Use the native <dialog> element when possible. Otherwise implement focus trapping, Escape to close, and focus restoration.

patterns.name: Tabs Missing ARIA Structure
patterns.description: Tab interfaces need proper ARIA roles and keyboard navigation.
patterns.codeBefore:
Tab 1
Tab 2
Content 1
Content 2
patterns.codeAfter:
Content 1
Content 2
patterns.notes: Keyboard: Arrow keys move between tabs, Tab moves to panel. Only selected tab is in tab order (others have tabindex="-1").

patterns.name: Insufficient Color Contrast
patterns.description: Text must have sufficient contrast against its background: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (AA).
patterns.notes: Large text is 18pt (24px) or 14pt (18.5px) bold. Use a contrast checker tool. Consider enhanced contrast (7:1/4.5:1) for AAA.

patterns.name: Color Used as Only Indicator
patterns.description: Information conveyed by color must also be available through other means like text, icons, or patterns.
patterns.codeBefore: Error in form Success
patterns.codeAfter: Error: Please correct the highlighted fields Success: Your form has been submitted
patterns.notes: Use icons, text labels, patterns, or underlines in addition to color. Ensure links are distinguishable from surrounding text without color.

patterns.name: Input Missing Autocomplete Attribute
patterns.description: Personal data input fields should have appropriate autocomplete attributes to help users fill forms.
patterns.codeBefore:
<input type="text" name="name">
<input type="email" name="email">
<input type="tel" name="phone">
patterns.codeAfter:
<input type="text" name="name" autocomplete="name">
<input type="email" name="email" autocomplete="email">
<input type="tel" name="phone" autocomplete="tel">
patterns.notes: Common values: name, email, tel, street-address, postal-code, cc-number, current-password, new-password. Helps users with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments.

patterns.name: Data Table Missing Headers
patterns.description: Data tables need proper header cells (th) with scope attributes to associate headers with data cells.
patterns.codeAfter:
Team members
Name Email Role
John john@example.com Admin
patterns.notes: Use th with scope="col" or scope="row". Add caption for table purpose. Use thead, tbody for structure. Complex tables may need headers/id attributes.

patterns.name: Page Language Not Specified
patterns.description: The page language must be specified so assistive technology can use correct pronunciation.
patterns.codeAfter:
<html lang="en">
  <head>...
patterns.notes: Use lang attribute on html element. For content in different languages, add lang to that element: Bonjour.
